proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed a matched finite-sample original-record risk and honest-length frontier with signed endpoint completion, bias/variance/arithmetic certificates, and legal multiscale alternatives. Independent mathematics and maximality audits passed after scope corrections and primary-source attestations; significance review graded subfield (7.2) below field (7.4), with no bounded faithful repair. tldr: Restricted win probability compares independent capped survival outcomes and gives half weight to a tie between horizon survivors. The proved original-record frontier matches finite-sample absolute risk and honest expected interval length uniformly in sample size, the public terminal-mass band and the known censor-tail exponent, including their joint critical transitions. Signed endpoint completion attains the rate, and legal full-record testing alternatives prove the converses. The connected intervals are finite-sample uniformly honest, with coverage at least \(0.90\). The converse transfers upward to larger containing classes under the same target and original-record experiment; upper guarantees apply to the prescribed class, and no sharp minimax or efficiency constant is claimed. The capped half-tie estimand and ordinary regular-regime procedures are inherited; the endpoint-degenerate censor regimes studied here are not covered by those regular conclusions.
gap: The inspected capped-win and censored-integral literature establishes regular asymptotic theory under fixed observation or integrability conditions. It does not supply a verified matched finite-sample absolute-risk and honest-length comparison through a public shrinking terminal atom and vanishing cap follow-up. This is an inferred scope boundary, not an open problem explicitly posed by those authors.
fill: The target result combines cutoff-dependent two-marginal certificates with full event-and-censor testing alternatives constrained by the same mass band. The resulting scalar precision function would inform prospective horizon and follow-up choices for the restricted-win clinical summary.
